That's useful. Your three picks all score well on a new metric I built from the references: dynamic range, sub-bass, and how often the track cuts to silence and then slams back in. Out of 154 tracks, **Come Closer, Don't Speak** ranks #1, **Autophagy** #11, and **Are We Doing This** #18. The metric roughly matches your taste, so I can use it to filter the next round.

I also need to correct something: **in the references you like most, the main drop comes late, about 65–75% of the way through, not at 28s.**

**Where the drop happens in the reference videos**

| Video | Length | Biggest moment | % through | What leads into it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Attio** | 47s | Big swell, peaking 30–34s | 64–72% | Sub-bass cuts out completely at 28.4s, about 1.5s of near-silence. Before that, a small bass thump on each word |
| **Raycast** | 39s | Slam at 28.3s | 73% | No single drop: 7 slams, each on a cut and each after a short dip (3.7, 8.9, 14, 17.8, 21.4, 24.2, 28.3s) |
| **Linear** | 55s | Hit at 42s | 76% | Opening hit at 4s, then a low bed |
| **Krea** | 67s | Drop at 50.5s | 75% | Silences at 31–33s and 48–50s |
| Rippling | 60s | Drop at 11s | 19% | A hard cut to silence first, then two more dropouts later |
| Notion / Claude / Hebbia | — | Drop at 13–17% | early | After that the groove stays flat |

In your favourites, the pattern is:
- Lots of small "cut to silence, then slam" hits on the cuts.
- The biggest hit around 70%, just after 1–2s of silence.
- The last 20–25% is a decaying tail under the logo.

For our 60s video, that means: slams every 3–6s, the main hit around **40–45s** with silence right before it, and a logo tail from about **47–60s**. My earlier "drop at 28s" came from Attio's black-screen moment, but at 28s Attio is actually in the silence before its big moment, and in a 47s video.

**How Autophagy compares**

| | Autophagy (60s cut) | References you like |
|---|---|---|
| Loudness range (LRA) | 2.1 LU | 11–13 LU |
| Punch (crest factor) | 9 dB | 14–16 dB |
| Sub-bass share | 58% | Raycast 54% |
| Drop position | 49% | about 70% |

So Autophagy has enough bass, but it's loud from the first second and stays flat, with one dropout at 24–29s. That's the "bassy but not dynamic" problem. (A wide loudness range means big swings between quiet and loud. A low crest factor means the track is heavily compressed, so hits don't stand out.)

**Why stock tracks fall short:** Attio's and Raycast's music was almost certainly scored to the picture, so their hits land on the cuts. A stock track won't do that. We can recreate it:
- Use the track's stems (separate bass, drums and melody parts) to mute the bass or drums for the dips.
- Add sub-hits, impacts and risers from Epidemic's sound effects for the slams.
- Place them on our cuts.

> Introducing Mila, your always-on AI deal desk. Get pricing, check buyer credit and prepare financing paperwork over email, Slack or chat. 24/7.

> Financing a software or hardware deal shouldn’t take longer than selling it. We built Mila so vendors on Capchase can go from quote to a financing proposal and ready-to-sign paperwork in one conversation.

Up until just ask I think it flows extremely well, but I think the script goes downhill from there.

The first half works because it's one story with real characters: Marcus is buried in emails and late-night pings, Mila arrives, and Acme signs. After "Just ask." the story stops and it turns into a string of slogans.

**What goes wrong after "Just ask."**

1. **"Just ask." repeats what we just saw.** We've watched Marcus ask Mila things for 14 seconds, so the line sums up rather than adding anything. The one new idea, that you can ask from email, Slack or finance.new, is only told with three chips, never shown.

3. **The deal rain is a show with no meaning.** It reads as "lots of deals", but whose deals, and what changed? It doesn't show "minutes" or "no matter how complex". It's the AI-slop risk again: impressive motion that says nothing specific.
4. **Loose threads.** Jordan's "Any update?", Marcus's "Was my buyer approved?" and David's "Need this ASAP." are never answered. That's the most satisfying payoff available, and we skip it.
5. **The end has no Mila line and no call to action.** "Vendor financing at the speed of tech." is Capchase's brand line, not the launch message. The blog's own lines are stronger here: "Need financing? Just talk to Mila." and "Have a quote ready? Ask Mila to price it → finance.new".
